lines: Hey Tom! It's been a while. How's your week going?
Pretty hectic, to be honest. We have a product launch next Monday.
Oh, that sounds stressful. Are you still commuting from Incheon?
Yes, it's about an hour each way, but I listen to podcasts on the train.
Nice. Can you recommend a good one? I need something for my commute too.
Sure, I'll send you a link. Let's catch up over lunch after the launch.

read.title: Why Small Talk Matters at Work
read.text:
Many people think small talk is a waste of time, but research suggests the opposite. Short, friendly conversations with colleagues can build trust and make it easier to ask for help later. A two-minute chat about someone's weekend or commute shows that you see them as a person, not just a job title.

The key is to ask open questions. Instead of "Did you have a good weekend?", try "What did you do this weekend?" Open questions invite longer answers and give you something to follow up on. Most importantly, listen more than you talk.

write.en: Write a short message to a colleague in an overseas office you haven't talked to in a while. Ask how they are and suggest coffee or lunch.

Hi Emma,
